```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

required_packages <- c("haven", "dplyr", "knitr")
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages)) {
  stop(
    "Instale los siguientes paquetes antes de generar el informe: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

library(haven)
library(dplyr)
```


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

data <- read.csv2(
  "retrauci_abril_2026.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = TRUE
)

source_file <- "FRANK-TODO.sav"
if (!file.exists(source_file)) {
  stop("No se encontro FRANK-TODO.sav en el directorio de trabajo.")
}

frank_original <- read_sav(source_file)

x <- filter(data, mais4 > 3 & is.na(mais3) )

dim(data)
```


```{r}

x <- intersect(frank_original$REGISTRO , data$registro )

```


## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
